newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal may have received Holocaust gold.
newsitem.headline: Portugal may have received Holocaust gold.

text.p: Gold stolen from Holocaust victims almost certainly figured amongst the tonnes of bullion received by Portugal from Nazi Germany in World War Two, a top Jewish official said on Tuesday.

World Jewish Congress (WJC) Assistant Secretary-General Maram Stern said so much gold was looted from Jews who died in Nazi concentration camps that it was unlikely that none of it turned up in shipments to Portugal.
Portugal was second only to Switzerland as a recipient of gold used by Germany to pay for goods bought during the 1939-45 war in which Lisbon was officially neutral.

"There was so much gold stolen. The logic would say 'yes'," Stern told Reuters when asked whether so-called "Holocaust gold" could be among consignments received during the war years by Portugal which was then under right-wing dictatorship.

With international Jewish organisations pressing for the truth over wartime gold trade, the Portuguese authorities have agreed to throw open state and central bank archives to investigators seeking to trace the flow of bullion.

Following the example of Switzerland, which has been rocked by accusations that it was effectively the Nazi regime's international banker, Portugal is setting up an independent commission to guide the investigations.
Portugal's gold reserves rose sixfold during the war years to some 356,000 tonnes, and according to U.S. intelligence documents the looted gold would be worth some $1.5 billion at today's prices.

Stern, who came to Portugal to discuss the investigations with the head of the Portuguese central bank and government officials, said that the WJC had readily accepted an offer to name a representative to the three-man commission.
He said the group would probably start work within the next two to three weeks with a first preliminary report being presented by October.
Stern praised what he called Portugal's clear commitment to answering all questions about the country's wartime activities, adding that he was convinced the truth would be known.
"I am sure that Portugal will do everything that it can to establish the truth," he said.

Documents uncovered in British and U.S. archives show that Portugal received several tonnes of gold looted from the Dutch and Belgian central banks after their countries were overrun by Nazi troops at the start of the war.

Some gold was returned by Lisbon in the 1950s as part of an international settlement covering bullion stolen from Nazi-occupied countries, but the deal made no mention of gold robbed from Holocaust victims.

Stern said that the question of what should be done if the investigators in Portugal concluded that some of the bullion must have come from jewellery, watches and even the teeth of murdered Jews was still to be tackled.
"The first thing we would expect would be recognition by Portugal of what had happened. Then there would be a discussion of what to do, but that would be more complex," he said.
